The credential strengthens your profile for promotion and moves you toward compensation levels that reward expertise and accountability.

content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Chicago

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a specific combination of formal education and verifiable project-management experience. Review PMI's baseline requirements—typically a bachelor's degree plus years of documented PM hours, or an associate degree with additional experience. Granite PM Academy's admissions team can verify your qualifications before enrollment, ensuring you're on track for application.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Our instructor-led course covers the entire PMBOK Guide framework and exam domains over a structured schedule. Attend from anywhere—all sessions are online, interactive, and designed for working Chicago professionals balancing career and study.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your formal education through Granite PM Academy, submit your PMP application directly to PMI, including proof of contact hours and your project-management experience documentation. Pay the required PMI exam fee at that time. Our team provides guidance on application requirements and deadlines to keep you moving forward.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor support—to build confidence before test day. Schedule your exam at a PMI-approved testing center. Our prep materials align directly with course content, helping you apply what you've learned to exam scenarios.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing the exam, maintain your certification by earning professional development units (PDUs) over a three-year renewal cycle. PMI offers many pathways to earn PDUs—training, volunteering, presenting, or publishing. Renewal keeps your credential current and signals your ongoing commitment to project-management excellence in your local job market.
